question: I missed the payment deadline because the transfer from my bank at home took 2 weeks. Will my classes be cancelled? How can I pay now

body.answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

Your classes may be deregistered (cancelled), but an outstanding balance does not always result in deregistration. The College says failure to pay in full may result in deregistration and a late fee; you will be notified via your Ramapo email if deregistered. [1][2] The Spring 2027 payment deadline is December 16, 2026. [13] Contact Student Accounts to confirm your account status and arrange payment.

You can pay online by electronic debit from a checking or savings account (ACH); these payments can only be made online. [14] For a bank wire transfer, Ramapo requires students to use PayMyTuition; initiate it at [https://payment.paymytuition.com/paynow/ramapo](https://payment.paymytuition.com/paynow/ramapo). [12] Other options include paying in person by cash, check, or money order at the Student Accounts office, or mailing a check or money order payable to Ramapo College. Include your nine-character Student ID number, beginning with “R”; do not mail cash. [5][6]

The Ramapo Tuition Payment Plan requires enrollment online through RCNJ Experience before the semester’s posted payment deadline; enrollment after the deadline requires missed installments at enrollment. [8] I don’t have verified information about whether your particular bank transfer qualifies as an exception; contact Student Accounts.

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [28]

This office can help:
**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [29]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/payment-policies/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deposits/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/paymytuition/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [29](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

When a student engages in or threatens to engage in such behavior, the most effective emergency response to protect the health and safety of the student and the community may be to require the student to leave the campus for a period of time. While an Interim Suspension is in place, the College will gather information and investigate the allegations(s) in order to make an individualized assessment of the risks posed by the student’s reported behavior and whether those risks may be mitigated to protect the health, safety, and learning environment of others. Where do I go if I have been issued an Interim Suspension? When you are Interim Suspended, you must vacate the campus. In cases when you are incapacitated (unable to act on your own), your emergency contact person is notified by the On Call Administrator. What if I am present on campus and violate the terms of the Interim Suspension? You will be considered trespassing and will be subjected to arrest by the Mahwah Police Department. The violation will be referred to the Office of Student Conduct. You will likely face on campus disciplinary charges and may also face charges through the Mahwah Municipal Court. What if I need to obtain clothing, books, medication, and other essential personal items from my residence room while I am serving an Interim Suspension? You need to contact Public Safety via phone at (201) 684-7432 to make arrangements to come to campus to gather any belongings from your residence. Do not come to campus without making prior arrangements. Am I able to attend classes when I am Interim Suspended? No, when you are serving an Interim Suspension, you are not permitted to physically attend classes. You are banned from entering the campus. Can I complete my coursework remotely? You may reach out to your faculty and ask if you may complete coursework electronically or by others means that do not require you to be present on the campus. The decision to accept coursework is under the purview of the individual faculty member who oversees the course material. answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

Your classes may be deregistered (cancelled), but an outstanding balance does not always result in deregistration. The College says failure to pay in full may result in deregistration and a late fee; you will be notified via your Ramapo email if deregistered. [1][2] The Spring 2027 payment deadline is December 16, 2026. [13] Contact Student Accounts to confirm your account status and arrange payment.

You can pay online by electronic debit from a checking or savings account (ACH); these payments can only be made online. [14] For a bank wire transfer, Ramapo requires students to use PayMyTuition; initiate it at [https://payment.paymytuition.com/paynow/ramapo](https://payment.paymytuition.com/paynow/ramapo). [12] Other options include paying in person by cash, check, or money order at the Student Accounts office, or mailing a check or money order payable to Ramapo College. Include your nine-character Student ID number, beginning with “R”; do not mail cash. [5][6]

The Ramapo Tuition Payment Plan requires enrollment online through RCNJ Experience before the semester’s posted payment deadline; enrollment after the deadline requires missed installments at enrollment. [8] I don’t have verified information about whether your particular bank transfer qualifies as an exception; contact Student Accounts.

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [28]

This office can help:
**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [29]

question: my landlord wants something that shows my financial aid for this semester bc im paying rent with the refund. can i get an award letter or something official

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status. Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

Financial Aid sends financial aid correspondence to your Ramapo College email. Check there for your College Financing Plan (CFP), which you’ll receive via email within a few weeks. [2][4]

The CFP provides an estimate of how much it may cost to attend college after your financial aid award. [5]

I don’t have verified information about obtaining an official letter specifically for your landlord. Contact Financial Aid.

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [32]

This office can help:
**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [33]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/calendar/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/understanding-your-financial-aid-award/spring-admits/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status. Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

Financial Aid sends financial aid correspondence to your Ramapo College email. Check there for your College Financing Plan (CFP), which you’ll receive via email within a few weeks. [2][4]

The CFP provides an estimate of how much it may cost to attend college after your financial aid award. [5]

I don’t have verified information about obtaining an official letter specifically for your landlord. Contact Financial Aid.

question: Are grad students allowed to go on the short winter break trips abroad? I'd like to sign up for one if there's still room

body.answer:
The Costa Rica Alternative Break trip is January 4–11, 2027, costs $975, and has capacity for 10 students. Applications closed October 14, 2026, so sign-up is closed. [18] The page does not say whether graduate students are eligible or whether there is still room; I don’t have verified information about that. Contact the Civic and Community Engagement Center. Applicants are not guaranteed a spot, as trips can be competitive. [17]

**Civic and Community Engagement Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7586. Email: ccec@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-213. [30]

Sources: [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/ccec/alternative/) [18](https://www.ramapo.edu/ccec/alternative/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i got a text with a login code when i tried to sign in over break, i never set that up?? is this a scam or do i need to do something

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [30]:
- Monday, September 7, 2026: Labor Day (College Closed - No Classes) (already passed)
- Wednesday, November 25, 2026: Thanksgiving Break (No Classes) (through November 29)
- Tuesday, December 8, 2026: Reading Day (No Classes)

Ramapo Gmail requires two-factor authentication. A code by text can be one of the verification methods, and when you sign in from a new device you may be prompted to verify your identity [4][6][9]. But if you didn’t initiate a sign-in, don’t share the code or approve a login you don’t recognize. The pages don’t say whether an unexpected code by itself means your account was accessed; contact the IT Help Desk for help [1].

**IT Help Desk**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: helpdesk@ramapo.edu. Location: 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [31]

question: is there like a career test i can take to figure out what to major in? i have to pick classes soon and have no clue

body.answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): A career test can highlight your interests, strengths, and work preferences, then suggest fields to explore. Treat the results as ideas—not a verdict—and compare them with majors’ courses, career paths, and what you enjoy learning. You can also use the results to guide conversations with people in those fields.

Yes. Ramapo lists FOCUS 2, an online, interactive career & education planning system that combines self-assessment, career exploration, and decision-making. It can help you map out a career path and select the right major area of study. Access code: ramapo430. [1]

The Career Assessments page also says assessments can help students find direction, explore future opportunities, and affirm career choices. Visit your Career Advisor for more information. [1]

Ramapo also publishes that the Cahill Career Development Center offers computer tests (Focus, Discover) to help you recognize your abilities, and that the Center for Student Success specializes in helping students choose majors. [17] Its goal is to help you choose the right major for you. [18]

To decide what classes to take, Ramapo suggests focusing on your top choices and choosing classes that help you make your decision; talk with faculty in those majors. [17]

- **Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [28]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [28]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/career-assessment/) [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [18](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): A career test can highlight your interests, strengths, and work preferences, then suggest fields to explore. Treat the results as ideas—not a verdict—and compare them with majors’ courses, career paths, and what you enjoy learning. You can also use the results to guide conversations with people in those fields.

Yes. Ramapo lists FOCUS 2, an online, interactive career & education planning system that combines self-assessment, career exploration, and decision-making. It can help you map out a career path and select the right major area of study. Access code: ramapo430. [1]

The Career Assessments page also says assessments can help students find direction, explore future opportunities, and affirm career choices. Visit your Career Advisor for more information. [1]

Ramapo also publishes that the Cahill Career Development Center offers computer tests (Focus, Discover) to help you recognize your abilities, and that the Center for Student Success specializes in helping students choose majors. [17] Its goal is to help you choose the right major for you. [18]

To decide what classes to take, Ramapo suggests focusing on your top choices and choosing classes that help you make your decision; talk with faculty in those majors. [17]

- **Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [28]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [28]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/career-assessment/) [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [18](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: got a note on my door about a health and safety inspection next week. what are they checking and do i have to be there

body.answer:
Residence Life inspections check that your room/suite/apartment, common area, bathroom, and bedroom are clean, healthy, and safe. They look for prohibited items, removed recyclables and garbage, cleaned bathroom/kitchen/living room and appliances, and bedrooms cleaned (vacuuming, removing garbage, wiping desk and dresser). They may also assess damage. [1][2]

You do not have to be there according to the information provided: authorized College personnel can enter rooms to conduct inspections. The exact date and time are not posted. [1]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [33]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: they told me i still have to take a placement test even though i already passed english comp at my old school?? why and how do i get out of it

body.answer:
If your transferred college-level English composition course satisfies Ramapo’s General Education Requirements, you are exempt from placement testing. [17] A student who has not completed the Critical Reading and Writing general education requirement through transfer credits may need a placement test to determine next steps. [19]

Ask Admissions whether your course and transcript meet the transfer-credit requirement. If the course is accepted as a direct equivalent to CRWT 080 or CRWT 090, completed with a grade of Pass or C (2.0) or better, Ramapo honors it as satisfying the remedial/developmental requirement; a transfer student meeting that requirement does not need retesting before registering for the subsequent college-level course. [26]

I don’t have verified information about the specific reason you were assigned a test or the process to appeal an assignment. Contact Admissions.

- **Testing Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: testing@ramapo.edu. Location: Laurel Hall, North. [28]
- **Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [28]

Sources: [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/eligibility/) [19](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/admitted-students/) [26](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#transferring-remedial-and-developmental-courses) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
If your transferred college-level English composition course satisfies Ramapo’s General Education Requirements, you are exempt from placement testing. [17] A student who has not completed the Critical Reading and Writing general education requirement through transfer credits may need a placement test to determine next steps. [19]

Ask Admissions whether your course and transcript meet the transfer-credit requirement. If the course is accepted as a direct equivalent to CRWT 080 or CRWT 090, completed with a grade of Pass or C (2.0) or better, Ramapo honors it as satisfying the remedial/developmental requirement; a transfer student meeting that requirement does not need retesting before registering for the subsequent college-level course. [26]

question: just transferred here this fall and i want to study abroad next year. is it too soon to apply? what do i have to do first

body.answer:
It’s not too soon to start: first complete the advisement questionnaire, then meet with the study abroad advisor, research program options, talk to Global Roadrunners, and complete the study abroad application. [1]

The Center recommends starting with the advisement questionnaire so it can best support you. [3] The specific application checklist depends on the program; items may include a $90 non-refundable application fee, essay, official Ramapo transcript, academic recommendation, course approval form, signed forms, emergency contact, and a copy of a valid passport. Your materials will not be reviewed until your application is complete. [4]

For details on when you can apply, contact the Roukema Center for International Education.

**Roukema Center for International Education**: Phone: (201) 684-7533. Location: C-wing, Suite 213. [25]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/study-abroad/getting-started/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/study-abroad/getting-started/virtual-advisement/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/study-abroad/application-process/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
It’s not too soon to start: first complete the advisement questionnaire, then meet with the study abroad advisor, research program options, talk to Global Roadrunners, and complete the study abroad application. [1]

The Center recommends starting with the advisement questionnaire so it can best support you. [3] The specific application checklist depends on the program; items may include a $90 non-refundable application fee, essay, official Ramapo transcript, academic recommendation, course approval form, signed forms, emergency contact, and a copy of a valid passport. Your materials will not be reviewed until your application is complete. [4]

question: My classes go until almost 10 and every dining spot is closed by then. Can I change my meal plan to just dining dollars or something like that?

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Late Night Dining is available at the Birch Tree Inn from 9 pm to 11pm Monday through Friday and 8 pm to 10pm Saturday and Sunday. You can access it as part of your Meal Plan or with Flex, Ramapo Dollars, cash or credit. [4]

Residents who wish to add a Block Plan or Flex Plan for Spring can request one beginning December 1, 2026. Email mealpan@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo College email account with your complete first and last name, Banner ID Number (R-Number), and plan of choice. Block and Flex plans DO NOT automatically roll over to the Spring semester, and are non-refundable. [6]

Students who wish to change their meal plan for Spring 2027 may do so through January 25, 2027. Email mealplan@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email account with the subject line: Spring 2027 Meal Plan Request. Include your complete first and last name, R-Number, and meal plan option. Requests take at least three business days to process; residents will receive a confirmation email once completed. Do not submit multiple email requests. [2] [3]

If you mean changing to a plan consisting only of dining dollars, I don't have verified information about whether that option is available. Contact Housing & Residence Life.

- **Dining Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7773. Location: Student Center, 1st Floor. [35]
- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [35]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/fallcheckoutandwinter/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/fallcheckoutandwinter/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Late Night Dining is available at the Birch Tree Inn from 9 pm to 11pm Monday through Friday and 8 pm to 10pm Saturday and Sunday. You can access it as part of your Meal Plan or with Flex, Ramapo Dollars, cash or credit. [4]

Residents who wish to add a Block Plan or Flex Plan for Spring can request one beginning December 1, 2026. Email mealpan@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo College email account with your complete first and last name, Banner ID Number (R-Number), and plan of choice. Block and Flex plans DO NOT automatically roll over to the Spring semester, and are non-refundable. [6]

Students who wish to change their meal plan for Spring 2027 may do so through January 25, 2027. Email mealplan@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email account with the subject line: Spring 2027 Meal Plan Request. Include your complete first and last name, R-Number, and meal plan option. Requests take at least three business days to process; residents will receive a confirmation email once completed. Do not submit multiple email requests. [2] [3]

If you mean changing to a plan consisting only of dining dollars, I don't have verified information about whether that option is available. Contact Housing & Residence Life.

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [35]

question: how do i set up direct deposit so my refund goes straight to my bank instead of a check

body.answer:
1. Log into RCNJ Experience: [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/) [1]
2. Locate the Student Account Info card and click Bill & Payment Suite. [1]
3. Click Electronic Refunds on the right hand side of the screen under the My Profile Setup menu. [1]
4. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if previously completed): in My Profile, click Security Settings, select a method to receive a passcode (text message, email or Google Authentication), click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify. [1]
5. In My Profile, click Payment Profile. Edit an existing saved Payment Method or Create New Payment Method. In either case, check the box in the Refund Option section to designate it as the refund account for direct deposit. [1]

You can expect an eligible refund to be deposited within one to two weeks of submitting the application. Eligibility applies to refunds from loan or financial-aid overpayment, or dropping classes within the appropriate add/drop dates. [2]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [32]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
1. Log into RCNJ Experience: [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/) [1]
2. Locate the Student Account Info card and click Bill & Payment Suite. [1]
3. Click Electronic Refunds on the right hand side of the screen under the My Profile Setup menu. [1]
4. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if previously completed): in My Profile, click Security Settings, select a method to receive a passcode (text message, email or Google Authentication), click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify. [1]
5. In My Profile, click Payment Profile. Edit an existing saved Payment Method or Create New Payment Method. In either case, check the box in the Refund Option section to designate it as the refund account for direct deposit. [1]

You can expect an eligible refund to be deposited within one to two weeks of submitting the application. Eligibility applies to refunds from loan or financial-aid overpayment, or dropping classes within the appropriate add/drop dates. [2]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [32]

question: does EOF have laptops we can borrow? mine died and finals are this week

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

I don’t have verified information about whether EOF lends laptops. The Library has five Lenovo PC laptops for current Ramapo students to borrow in the library; loans are for 2 hours and may be renewed for another 2 hours depending on demand. Check them out at the Circulation Desk. They are in-house use only. [1]

Laptop Upcycle @ Ramapo also accepts requests from currently enrolled students. Apply using the [We Care Program Application Form](https://www.ramapo.edu/ccec/we-care-program-application/). You must be a current undergraduate or graduate student, enrolled part-time or full-time, in good standing with the Office of Student Conduct, and have demonstrated financial need confirmed by the Office of Financial Aid. Applying does not guarantee a laptop. [17]

For an EOF-specific answer, contact the Educational Opportunity Fund (EOF) Program.

- **Library**: Phone: (201) 684-7575. Email: circ@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons. [31]
- **Laptop Upcycle @ Ramapo**: Email: laptopupcycle@ramapo.edu. [31]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/computers-and-laptops/) [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/upcycle/request-device/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i missed my advising appointment yesterday 😬 and i think i need it before i can register. can i reschedule

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

Yes. Find the appointment in your Upcoming Appointments channel on Connect’s home page, click the calendar icon at the beginning of the line, then choose edit or cancel. To book a new time, go to web.ramapo.edu and click the red Connect button. In Connect, open My Success Network, click your advisor’s name, choose an available time using the Sign Up link, complete the form, and click Save. You’ll receive an email confirmation. If your faculty advisor doesn’t have a Connect calendar set up, email them for an appointment. [3][4][2]

You don’t generally have to meet with an advisor before registering, except Contemporary Arts and Environmental Science students must consult their assigned faculty advisor before registration each Spring. Second-year students in the Fall have an advisement hold and must meet with their faculty advisor before registering for Winter and Spring; undeclared students should see their faculty advisor, who lifts the hold after meeting. [7][8]

If you’re unsure whether you have a hold, check with the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising).

**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [32]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/connect/students/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/connect/students/frequently-asked-questions/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/connect/students/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I have accommodations for extra time but my two summer finals are on the same day and both are long. Can I take one of them on a different day?

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

If you have two finals on the same day, the policy does not provide rescheduling based on exam length or extra-time accommodations. It says students are not expected to take more than two exams or other culminating assessments on one day. If scheduled for more than two, you must take the earliest and latest at their assigned times and may request that the middle exam(s) be rescheduled. Faculty must accommodate that request if made by the end of the third class meeting scheduled during summer terms. [22]

I don’t have verified information about whether your extra-time accommodations would allow you to reschedule one of two finals; contact the Office of Specialized Services.

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [25]

Sources: [22](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#final-examinations-and-other-culminating-assessments) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I'm back home in India for winter break. Can I still book a session with a counselor online from here?

body.answer:
The academic calendar doesn't list a winter break by name. Between the Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 semesters it lists [31]:
- Tuesday, December 15, 2026: Full and Session II Courses - Last Day of the Semester
- Thursday, December 17, 2026: First Day of Winter Classes
- Tuesday, January 19, 2027: Full and Session I Courses - Classes Begin

Yes. Uwill offers free, immediate access to teletherapy and lists international coverage. [20] To book, go to [https://app.uwill.com/](https://app.uwill.com/) and complete your profile using your school email address and current location; you can then immediately schedule an appointment with a therapist of your choosing. [2] You can choose a therapist based on preferences including availability, issue, gender, language, and ethnicity, and select a time with day, night, and weekend availability. [1]

**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [32]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/uwill/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/uwill/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/access-to-mental-health-support/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

It’s important to understand that each culture and country has its own systems of functioning. You may appreciate certain aspects of your host culture but dislike others. The same is likely true of your perspective of the U.S. now that you’ve returned. Re-entry is different for everyone. question: my EOF counselor said the grant won't cover my summer class. i dont get why, isnt summer part of the year? is there anything i can do

body.answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

The EOF grant for the Pre-Freshman Summer Studies Institute is specifically described as covering that program’s costs; the pages don’t say the grant automatically covers any summer class. The EOF Program says EOF students may apply for assistance for summer session tuition and fees, and that additional assistance depends on available funds. [2][14]

Ask the EOF Office about applying for summer-course assistance. [14]

**Educational Opportunity Fund (EOF) Program**: Phone: (201) 684-7541. Email: EOFdesk@ramapo.edu. Office: D-101. [33]

These offices can help:
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [34]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [34]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/financial/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/educational-opportunity-fund/admission-requirements/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

The EOF grant for the Pre-Freshman Summer Studies Institute is specifically described as covering that program’s costs; the pages don’t say the grant automatically covers any summer class. Ask the EOF Office about applying for summer-course assistance. [14]

body.answer:
You can move the appointment yourself through the appointment system, or email the Testing Center and they can assist. [1]

For remote Accuplacer placement testing, appointments must be made at least 2 business days in advance. The sign-up form shows available test days and times. [3]

**Testing Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: testing@ramapo.edu. Location: Laurel Hall, North. [25]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/clep/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/testing/remote/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: my parents gave me a different car over break, how do i change the car on my parking permit before i come back

body.answer:
Remove the permit from the old car, affix it to the new vehicle, and email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu with the updated vehicle information. If the permit is damaged or will no longer adhere to the window, bring it to the Public Safety Parking and ID Office, Rm. C101, to swap it at no cost for a new permit. [1]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [32]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [32]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: Two of my classes overlap by 15 minutes on Tuesday. The system let me register but I can't be in both. I need to stay full time for my visa. What should I do?

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

The Registrar’s guidance for overlapping class times is: “Select another course.” [8] Check for an alternate course or section, and contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) for help reviewing your remaining requirements and options. [1]

If you are an F-1 student, you must register for a complete full course load every semester—at least 12 credits for undergraduate students, or ordinarily 9 credits for graduate students. [22] Obtain ISSS approval before finalizing any registration for a reduced course load; retroactive approval once registration has ended is not possible. [22] Consult ISSS about your F-1 status, and contact the Registrar about the schedule conflict.

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [36]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [36]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/registration-faq/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/current/) [36](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I work part time in the dining hall and my new landlord wants proof of my job and how much I make. Who in dining can write that?

body.answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

People Operations and Employee Resources Department is the only department authorized to respond to employment verification inquiries. It can confirm dates of employment, salary, and position(s) held. The verification is usually provided within 48 hours of receipt, and requires a written authorization and release signed by you. **People Operations and Employee Resources Department**: Phone: (201) 684-7506. Email: poer@ramapo.edu. Location: D-wing. [31]

question: My employer reimburses tuition but they need an official paper showing I finished my summer course with a grade. Where do I get that?

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

For an official paper showing your course and grade, request an official transcript online through the Registrar’s website: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/) [7].

You can view grades online shortly after the semester ends: log in through the Experience Webapp ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), select “FINAL GRADES” under the Student Records Menu, then select “Term” to view grades [21].

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [37]

Sources: [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/asb/essentials/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [37](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: is there scholarship money for grad students going abroad? i want to apply before the deadline if there is

body.answer:
Yes. Ramapo lists scholarships and other financial resources for study abroad, including the Boren Scholarship, Gilman Scholarship, Critical Language Scholarship, and Fulbright U.S. Student Program. The Fulbright U.S. Student Program supports graduate study and research in over 140 countries; graduating seniors or graduate students may apply, and grants include book allowances, tuition, transportation, and a moderate dependence allowance. Applicants must meet the language requirements of the award. [2][18][20]

The General Application is the first step to qualify for scholarships. [17] The 26/27 academic-year application deadline was September 23, 2026, so it has passed. [17] For other opportunities and deadlines, check the scholarship websites and the Ramapo scholarship updates, or contact the Roukema Center for International Education.

- **Transportation Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: shuttle@ramapo.edu. [32]
- **Roukema Center for International Education**: Phone: (201) 684-7533. Location: C-wing, Suite 213. [32]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/study-abroad/scholarships/) [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/scholarships/faqs/) [18](https://www.ramapo.edu/prestigious-fellowships-and-scholarships/single/fulbright-u-s-student-program/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/prestigious-fellowships-and-scholarships/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I can't find a library book I borrowed and finals are here. What happens if I lost it, do I just pay for it?

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

If you cannot find the book, ask Circulation staff for assistance. Complete the missing-book form available at the Circulation Desk; staff will search for the book and notify you of the outcome. [3]

For a book not returned 28 days after its due date, a $75.00 charge applies ($50 replacement fee and $25 processing fee). It is billed to your Office of Student Accounts account. Outstanding charges of $75 or more suspend borrowing privileges; transcripts and diplomas may also be held until the charges are resolved. [1]

For questions about book charges, contact Madel Tisi at mtisi@ramapo.edu or Lili Pasaporte at lpasapor@ramapo.edu. [1]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [24]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/circulation/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/circulation/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i got a bill from a lab for bloodwork the health center sent out. i thought it was free?? who do i ask about this

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Laboratory work is subject to normal deductibles and copays, even if it is drawn at Ramapo College Health Services. The 100% coverage applies only to covered services, such as routine primary care and preventive services; it does not mean all medical care is free. [1]

Ask Health Services about the lab referral and bill. [3]

**Health Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7536. Location: Near the campus South Gate entrance at the corner of Route 202 and Hornbeam Road. [33]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/student-health-insurance/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Damage charges are assessed as a result of depreciating the value of the item that belongs to the college; not necessarily to be able to replace something or repair it to its original value. If more than one student occupies a space in which damage/loss occurs, the students will be held equally liable, unless one or more takes responsibility for the damage/loss. If damage/loss does occur, it is helpful if the residents notify the hall office (via email is recommended) to ensure that billing is correct and the circumstances surrounding the damage/loss known. What is Preventive Care? Preventive care focuses on maintaining your health, and establishing your baseline health status. This may include immunizations, vaccines, physical evaluations, lab work, x-rays and medically appropriate health screenings. During your preventive visit, your doctor will determine what tests or screenings are appropriate for you based on many factors such as your age, gender, overall health status, personal health history and your current symptoms or chronic health concerns. Click the link to access the Preventive Health Guidelines for both Children and Adults. Preventive_Health_Guidelines (https://www.ramapo.edu/poerd/wp-content/uploads/sites/62/2013/04/Preventive_Health_Guidelines.pdf) Grand Rounds Health: NJ SHBP Expert Medical Opinion Partner What is Grand Rounds Health? Grand Rounds Health is a remote expert second opinion partner that connects SHBP and SEHBP participants to world-class experts for expert guidance for members with complex needs. This benefit helps improve outcomes and reduce costs from incorrect diagnoses and treatment. Grand Rounds Health services are available at no out-of-pocket costs. How do members get started? Eligible plan members can visit www.grandrounds.com/shbp (http://www.grandrounds.com/shbp) or call 1-855-734-4017 to enroll. They can access their account on any device (desktop, tablet, or mobile) after they sign up. What can members do with Grand Rounds Health? Receive an expert second opinion for a world-class expert for any condition they may have which included Grand Rounds Health gathering all available medical records on behalf of the member. question: I'm in EOF and signed up to be a peer mentor for the summer program but I just got a job offer. Can I do only part of it or do I have to drop out

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

The EOF Program says students are expected to attend all classes, workshops, meetings, and activities unless otherwise approved by EOF staff. If you cannot fully participate, you can request admission to Ramapo as a non-EOF student. Once on campus, you can apply to join the EOF Internal Transfer waitlist; students accepted through it do not receive the Ramapo College Grant. [3] Contact the Educational Opportunity Fund (EOF) Program to ask whether staff will approve your partial participation. [3]

**Educational Opportunity Fund (EOF) Program**: Phone: (201) 684-7541. Email: EOFdesk@ramapo.edu. Office: D-101. [14]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/freshman/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: my friend from home wants to visit and stay over in my room this weekend. do i have to register her somewhere

body.answer:
Yes. Since your friend is not a current Ramapo residential student, if she is 18 or older and will be on campus after 10:00 PM, she needs to complete Guest Registration; she may be registered any night of the week. She must have valid ID and access to the approved Guest Registration email, and remain with you at all times. [3]
A registered guest may stay no more than three nights (consecutively or not) within a seven-day period; nights begin and end at 10:00 PM. You may host up to two guests at a time. [2]
Overnight guests are permitted through Monday, December 14, 2026; they are not permitted after that date. [6]
I don’t have verified information about registration requirements if your friend is under 18. Contact Housing & Residence Life. [3]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [34]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/fallcheckoutandwinter/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

She must have valid ID and access to the approved Guest Registration email, and remain with you at all times. [3]

question: is there a way to do bachelors and masters together in 5 years? i'd want to sign up early if thats a thing

body.answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers 4+1 pathways that let eligible students complete a bachelor’s and master’s in five years. Undergraduates majoring in Computer Science, Data Science, Cybersecurity, Mathematics, and Bioinformatics can enroll in the Center of DMC’s MS pathways and take graduate courses as seniors. [1] There are also other 4+1 options, including Accounting, MBA, and Public Policy. [6][4][7]

To sign up for the DMC 4+1 program, complete the [4+1 Declaration Form](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/04/41-Declaration-Form-FILLABLE.pdf) and return it to sfrees@ramapo.edu. [3] You can enroll anytime before your last two semesters before undergraduate graduation, typically before spring semester junior year. [5] Contact the graduate program director for additional enrollment information and guidelines. [17]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [32]

question: Everyone keeps talking about Handshake but I don't know what it is. Do I need it to find a job on campus?

body.answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Handshake is an online platform where students and recent graduates can find internships and jobs, explore employers, and connect with recruiters. It’s often used by colleges to share career opportunities with their students.

Handshake is Ramapo’s job bank and online career management system. [9] It also lets students apply for internships and jobs, register for career fairs and events, and schedule Career Center appointments. [3]

Yes—register on Handshake to view open on-campus positions. Search using the keyword ‘RCNJ’; follow the instructions in each posting and contact the listed supervisor. [24]

answer:
**General answer** (from general knowledge, not Ramapo's pages): Handshake is an online platform where students and recent graduates can find internships and jobs, explore employers, and connect with recruiters. It’s often used by colleges to share career opportunities with their students.

Handshake is Ramapo’s job bank and online career management system. [9] It also lets students apply for internships and jobs, register for career fairs and events, and schedule Career Center appointments. [3]

Yes—register on Handshake to view open on-campus positions. Search using the keyword ‘RCNJ’; follow the instructions in each posting and contact the listed supervisor. [24]

**Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [30]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/faculty-staff/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/employer/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i get assigned an advisor? im undeclared and nobody ever contacted me

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Undeclared students are assigned to professional advisors in the Center for Student Success through the Ramapo Exploration Program. [7][11] Check your Connect network to find your assigned advisor; it is updated during the first month of each semester. [6][10] You can also use the [Connect guides](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/how-to-guides/) to find your designated advisor and schedule an appointment. [14]

Since nobody has contacted you, contact the Center for Student Success for advisement. [13]

**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [28]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/te/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/how-to-guides/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I'm signed up for 2 classes in my masters program for spring but I want to go down to 1 because of work. Is that allowed? I'm afraid of losing my aid

body.answer:
I don’t have verified information about whether taking one class is allowed for your particular master’s program. Contact your program’s academic advisor to confirm. [7][8]

For financial aid, the effect depends on your credits and aid type. Federal aid requires 6 credits in a semester; if you go from 12 credits to 6, your federal Pell Grant will be reduced, but you can keep your federal loans. State aid may be canceled, and institutional grants and scholarships could be reduced or taken away. [8] If you remain enrolled in 6 or more credits, federal aid should not be affected; NJ State aid, including TAG and EOF, requires full-time enrollment when it is fully disbursed to your account. [7] Meet with the Office of Financial Aid before changing your enrollment to discuss the possible impact on your current aid package. [7][8]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [23]

Sources: [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
I don’t have verified information about whether taking one class is allowed for your particular master’s program. Contact your program’s academic advisor to confirm. [7][8]

For financial aid, the effect depends on your credits and aid type. Federal aid requires 6 credits in a semester; if you go from 12 credits to 6, your federal Pell Grant will be reduced, but you can keep your federal loans. State aid may be canceled, and institutional grants and scholarships could be reduced or taken away. [8] If you remain enrolled in 6 or more credits, federal aid should not be affected; NJ State aid, including TAG and EOF, requires full-time enrollment when it is fully disbursed to your account. [7] Meet with the Office of Financial Aid before changing your enrollment to discuss the possible impact on your current aid package. [7][8]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [23]

Sources: [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

body.answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

Check your printing usage and funds at [http://print.ramapo.edu](http://print.ramapo.edu). [1] Each student receives 200 pages per academic year at no charge; the allowance resets at the beginning of each academic year (each fall semester). [2]

I don’t have verified information about disputing an unauthorized printing charge or securing your account. Contact the IT Help Desk, which can help with printing problems. [21]

**IT Help Desk**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: helpdesk@ramapo.edu. Location: 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [35]

These offices can help:
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [36]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [36]

question: I lost my I-20 and I think my passport was in the same folder. What do I do first?

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Contact the Roukema Center for International Education first about your lost I-20 and passport. Ramapo’s guidance says to contact the office immediately about travel document issues, and to carry original documents when traveling outside New Jersey. [12][20]

**Roukema Center for International Education**: Phone: (201) 684-7533. Location: C-wing, Suite 213. [30]

Sources: [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/immigration-updates/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/public-safety-frequently-asked-questions/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: My parking ticket was due last week and I forgot about it. Now there's a late fee. Can I still pay it online?

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Yes. Pay online through the [Payment Portal](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx). Enter Citation # and Fine Amount, search for the citation, select your citation and follow the field required, then select a payment method. Once processed, your citation will be emailed to you to say that it is paid. [4]

Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee. A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days. [1]

If the fine has not been transferred to your student account, first stop at the Parking and ID Office, Rm. C101, or contact parking services at parking@ramapo.edu to ensure that it has been transferred. During regular business hours, payments may be made to the Office of Student Accounts. [1]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [31]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I am new international student starting in January. When should I arrive and who do I tell when I land?

body.answer:
Plan to arrive on or before the report date listed on your I-20 or DS-2019; you must report to the Roukema Center for International Education no later than 15 days after that date to complete mandatory check-in. [2] Do not arrive in the U.S. more than 30 days before the reported date on your I-20 or DS-2019. [5]

Tell the Office of International Students and Scholars as early as possible your airline name, flight number(s), departure and arrival times, and names of both departure and arrival airports. The page says the easiest way is email: iosawami@ramapo.edu. [4] When you land, report to the Roukema Center for International Education for check-in. [2]

**Roukema Center for International Education**: Phone: (201) 684-7533. Location: C-wing, Suite 213. [28]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/orientation/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/transfer/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/orientation/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I see a counselor on campus but I'm home in another state for break. Can we still meet on video or is that not allowed?

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [32]:
- Monday, September 7, 2026: Labor Day (College Closed - No Classes) (already passed)
- Wednesday, November 25, 2026: Thanksgiving Break (No Classes) (through November 29)
- Tuesday, December 8, 2026: Reading Day (No Classes)

Counseling appointments are conducted in person or via telehealth using a secure platform for audio/video communication between students and counselors [3]. Ongoing individual therapy is offered in person or via telehealth [4]. The pages do not say whether you can attend telehealth sessions while you are physically in another state; I don’t have verified information about that. Contact the Counseling Center to confirm.

**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [33]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/faq/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i get into the library databases from home? it keeps asking me to log in and my login doesnt work

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Use the library’s [Databases A–Z](https://libguides.ramapo.edu/az/databases) page to open databases; off campus, links without the library’s proxy prefix won’t authenticate. Sign in with your Ramapo email username and password. Your username should not include “@ramapo.edu,” and you must be a current student, faculty member, or staff member. Alumni and non-College courtesy borrowers cannot access these materials off campus. Your browser must accept cookies. [1][2][4]

If it still fails, check your spelling and make sure Caps Lock is off. Try logging out of any VPN, clearing browser history/cache/cookies, another browser or device, or a different internet connection. [2][4]

For technical problems, see the [troubleshooting guide](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/off-campus-access-troubleshooting/) or contact the IT Help Desk.

- **Library**: Phone: (201) 684-7575. Email: circ@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons. [23]
- **IT Help Desk**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: helpdesk@ramapo.edu. Location: 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [23]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/off-campus-access-instructions/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/off-campus-access-troubleshooting/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/off-campus-access-troubleshooting/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Use the library’s [Databases A–Z](https://libguides.ramapo.edu/az/databases) page to open databases; off campus, links without the library’s proxy prefix won’t authenticate. Sign in with your Ramapo email username and password. Your username should not include “@ramapo.edu,” and you must be a current student, faculty member, or staff member. Alumni and non-College courtesy borrowers cannot access these materials off campus. Your browser must accept cookies. [1][2][4]

If it still fails, check your spelling and make sure Caps Lock is off. Try logging out of any VPN, clearing browser history/cache/cookies, another browser or device, or a different internet connection. [2][4]

For technical problems, see the [troubleshooting guide](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/off-campus-access-troubleshooting/) or contact the IT Help Desk.

- **Library**: Phone: (201) 684-7575. Email: circ@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons. [23]
- **IT Help Desk**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: helpdesk@ramapo.edu. Location: 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [23]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/off-campus-access-instructions/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/off-campus-access-troubleshooting/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/off-campus-access-troubleshooting/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: the counseling appointment form wont submit, it just keeps spinning. is there another way to make an appointment

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

For an initial triage appointment, call 201-684-7522. The appointment is in person and scheduled for 60 minutes. [1]

You can also register with Uwill at [https://app.uwill.com/](https://app.uwill.com/) using your school email, complete your profile with your current location, and schedule directly with a therapist. [2][3]

For a brief, confidential drop-in, no appointment is needed. Drop-ins are Monday–Friday, 1–3 pm in Academic Building D, room 216; call 201-684-7522 during drop-in hours for in-person or telehealth. The last meeting begins at 2:40 pm. [4]

**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [31]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/uwill/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/uwill/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/counseling/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

For an initial triage appointment, call 201-684-7522. The appointment is in person and scheduled for 60 minutes. [1]

You can also register with Uwill at [https://app.uwill.com/](https://app.uwill.com/) using your school email, complete your profile with your current location, and schedule directly with a therapist. [2][3]

For a brief, confidential drop-in, no appointment is needed. Drop-ins are Monday–Friday, 1–3 pm in Academic Building D, room 216; call 201-684-7522 during drop-in hours for in-person or telehealth. The last meeting begins at 2:40 pm. [4]

question: advisor said my stats class from my last school only counts as an elective not for my major. i dont get it, its the same class. can i ask for someone to look at it again

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're going through that. It's okay to not be okay, and you don't have to handle it alone.

Yes. If approval for a non-general-education course equivalency has not been established, you may contact the Convener of the appropriate program to review the course and its potential for transfer credit. If the Convener approves the equivalency, approval goes to the Office of Admissions, which designates someone to update the appropriate systems. [4]

For a psychology course, arrange to meet with the psychology convener and bring a copy of your detailed degree audit and the course syllabus. The convener reviews whether it meets Ramapo program requirements; if approved, they complete and sign a Course Equivalency Form, which you deliver to the Registrar’s Office. [1]

I don’t have verified information about who the appropriate convener is for your major. Contact the School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office if you are in Psychology, or your program’s convener for another major. [1][4]

- **Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [32]
- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [32]

This office can help:
**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [33]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/psychology/faqs/) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#transferring-academic-credit1) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

The grade replacement option is only available four times total during a student’s undergraduate academic career at the College.
The grade replacement option is only available two times total during a student’s graduate academic career at the College.
Grade replacement might not be available for a course in which an academic integrity violation occurred and the sanction was an F; students should consult their sanction letter, the Academic Integrity policy (https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3) and/or the Vice Provost for additional information. A grade replacement is not reversible once processed to the student’s academic transcript.
All grade replacements must be processed before graduation. Once a student graduates, a grade replacement cannot be applied, as no changes of any kind can be made to the academic record.
Courses and types of courses eligible for grade replacement:
The course must bear the same subject, course number, and title as the course that is being replaced.In cases where the course being replaced has been discontinued and is no longer active, the student may request the grade replacement be issued for the equivalent renumbered course should one exist (e.g.1, if SOSC 101 has been discontinued and its equivalent renumbered course is SOSC 110; e.g.2, if the 4-credit BIOL 110 lecture/lab has been discontinued and its two equivalent renumbered courses are the 4-credit BIOL 111 lecture plus the 1-credit BIOL 111L lab).A student cannot use a grade replacement for a discontinued course that is no longer offered and for which there is no equivalent course.
The course may carry the same number or a different number of credits.
A student may use a grade replacement for an Independent Study or a Topics course, provided that it is the same course (including the same course level). Approval of the Dean (and Program Director for graduate students) is required. Examples:A student enrolls in an IS, performs poorly, and retakes the same IS to attempt a better grade; grade replacement is permissible. The same IS number & name must be used.When an IS is substituting for a regular course (e.g., due to low enrollment), and the IS is a version of the regular course, grade replacement is permissible. B – Second Bachelors – Students who have completed a Bachelor’s Degree in another discipline and who have been admitted to a program that leads to the completion of a second Bachelor’s degree.
G – Graduate – Students who have been accepted and plan to matriculate in a graduate level program.
I – Internal Transfer – Undergraduate students who have been attending Ramapo College as non-matriculated students who are accepted to and plan to matriculate into a degree program.

A cross-listed course is a single course with a single title that has two or more course subjects and ID numbers by which it is listed in two or more programs at the college; if the ID numbers are not identical, they must however be at the same level.
There are instances in which cross-listing of courses would strengthen the curriculum. Cross-listing courses either within or between schools would have the primary function of promoting interdisciplinary education at the college.
There must be a clear curricular benefit for a course to be cross-listed; this benefit should be determined at the level of the programs considering cross-listing, and may take many different forms. For instance, an interdisciplinary program that includes disciplinary courses in its lists of courses that satisfy major category requirements may wish to cross-list certain disciplinary courses that meet a criteria of interdisciplinarity; the program could then require students to take a set number of courses that are either listed or cross-listed with its own course ID prefix, improving the interdisciplinary quality of the major.
Additional requirements for cross-listed courses
A course may be cross-listed between or among programs in the same school or in different schools and could occur within either undergraduate or graduate programs.
A cross-listed course must have a primary home in one program which will be responsible for scheduling, staffing, and assessing the course. A cross-listed course cannot be offered without approval of the program in which it is primarily housed.
If a cross-listed course is a requirement for its secondary program then that program must be notified of any modifications to the course so that it can determine if cross-listing should continue.
A cross-listed course may be taught in multiple sections as long as the course content and learning outcomes for all sections are the same.
All pre-requisites for a course remain in place for all students taking that course when it is cross-listed.
The subject codes for the course ID numbers should reflect the course content.
A student will receive credit only once for taking a cross-listed course and cannot switch from one course ID to the other after the add/drop period has ended.
An independent study or "Topics" course cannot be cross-listed.
For a course to be cross-listed (or to be un-crosslisted) it must be reviewed and approved as follows:
The convening group of each program concerned, in agreement with all instructors of the course, reviews and approves the cross-listing.

question: I graduate in May and just found out I should have applied for OPT already?? Is it too late and what do I do

body.answer:
I don’t have verified information on whether it’s too late for May graduation; contact the Roukema Center for International Education right away. [1][6]

If you are in valid F-1 status and have completed at least one academic year (two semesters) of full-time study, you may be eligible for OPT. [1] The Center must first recommend you for off-campus employment on Form I-20. Then file Form I-765, “Application for Employment Authorization,” with USCIS. If approved, USCIS will issue an EAD. You may not begin work until you have received the EAD. [6]

The OPT Form is here: [https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/wp-content/uploads/sites/232/2013/11/opt-form.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/wp-content/uploads/sites/232/2013/11/opt-form.pdf) [3]

**Roukema Center for International Education**: Phone: (201) 684-7533. Location: C-wing, Suite 213. [33]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/current/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/inter-students/forms/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/dmc/international-students/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I stay on campus over winter break and my meal swipes don't work at the dining hall. How do I get food?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that. You're not alone, and you can ask for help.

If you’re experiencing food insecurity, apply to the Swipe Out Hunger Program for 5 meals to use at the Birch Tree Inn. The program is limited; students with Ultimate or Maroon 14 plans are not eligible. New applicants and students without a meal plan receive priority; repeat applicants may be considered case by case. Apply here: [https://cglink.me/2fF/s60806](https://cglink.me/2fF/s60806). Questions: wecare@ramapo.edu. [10]

You can also take free grab-and-go items from campus satellite pantries. For more items or a larger selection, stop by the food pantry in ASB 130. [12]

**Civic and Community Engagement Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7586. Email: ccec@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-213. [32]

question: I want to drop one class but then I would have only 9 credits. Can I drop it and add a different one this week?

body.answer:
You can add or drop courses only before or within the first week of classes. After add/drop ends, you can no longer add classes to your schedule. Check the academic calendar for the deadline: [https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [1]

Nine credits is part-time; full-time is 12–18 credits. [29] Dropping below full-time may affect financial aid; federal aid requires at least 6 credits, and state aid, grants, or scholarships may be reduced or canceled. [3] Seek advisement before dropping, since this may also affect graduation progress, athletic compliance, housing, and campus activities. [6] Contact Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) for advice and Financial Aid about your aid.

- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [35]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [35]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [29](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/returning-student/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: lost my phone and now i cant get the login code for my school account. how do i get back in

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Contact the IT Help Desk for help getting back into your account. [2][13]

Ramapo Gmail requires 2FA. [5][11]

**IT Help Desk**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: helpdesk@ramapo.edu. Location: 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [33]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/mfa/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/email-activation-and-information/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/mfa/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/important-notes-for-password-reset/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

calls.given: {"today": "Wednesday, November 18, 2026", "now": "11:31 AM", "question": "lost my phone and now i cant get the login code for my school account. how do i get back in", "contacts_written_by_code": true, "offices": [{"office": "Dean of Students", "email": ["deanofstudents@ramapo.edu"], "phones": [[{"number": "+12016847457"}, {"type": "Fax", "number": "+12016847963"}]], "rooms": [["C-212"]], "sections": [{"n": 1, "heading": "How to Access Your Ramapo E-Mail as of February 28th", "page": "https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/how-to-access-your-ramapo-e-mail-as-of-february-28th/", "text": "To: All Students From: Melissa Van Der Wall, Dean of Students Date: February 24, 2023 Dear Students, I write to remind you of timely information stemming from Information Technology Services (ITS). ITS has installed a new feature designed for web security called Two-Factor Authentication, otherwise known as 2FA. Please be sure to follow the instructions so that you can maintain access to your email as of February 28, 2023. What is 2FA? According to Microsoft, two-factor authentication is a security system that requires two separate, distinct forms of identification in order to access something (in this case, your Ramapo Gmail). You may be familiar with 2FA with your banking accounts as you provide your user name, passcode, and then are texted with a security code to enter. What do I need to do? As of February 28, 2023, 2FA will be required in order to access Ramapo Gmail. If you have not already set up your account in preparation for 2FA, then please follow the instructions provided by ITS at this link (https://web.ramapo.edu/its/google-2fa-requirement/) as soon as possible. If you do not complete the set-up prior to February 28th, you could lose access to email temporarily until it is restored. What if I do not set up 2FA? You will not have access to your Ramapo email account and this will impact your learning experience at Ramapo. I set up 2FA, so what happens on February 28th? On February 28th, when you log in to your email, you will be prompted to open the Gmail app on your phone and approve the login. You will be able to trust the device so you do not have to do this every time. Only trust your personal device. Never trust a public computer. Do you need technical help? Please reach out to the ITS Help Desk at 201-684-7777 or email helpdesk@ramapo.edu (mailto:helpdesk@ramapo.edu). The email account is monitored and responded to Monday-Thursday from 8:00am to 8:00pm and Friday from 8:00am to 4:30pm. The 2FA extra layer is an important element toward giving you more protected online account security. Criminal activity and malicious attacks are a reality that we are all living with, so we must take important and proactive steps toward protecting ourselves. This will open the side bar. Scroll down and select “settings”. Select your account at the top, and tap on “Your info, privacy, and security”. This will take you to your Google account settings. Google Account Settings screenshot (https://www.ramapo.edu/its/wp-content/uploads/sites/102/2026/02/3gmail2fa_blurred.jpg) From there, tap on the Security tab. There it will show you recommended settings and other information about your account, devices, etc. Scroll down to “Signing in to Google”, you will see a sub-selection that says “2-Step Authentication”. question: my aid for spring looks way lower than fall and i didnt change anything. how do i find out why and fix it

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status. Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

Check whether your enrollment changed: dropping below full-time can adjust aid. Federal aid requires 6 credits; if you go from 12 credits to 6, your federal Pell may be reduced, though you can keep federal loans. State aid may be canceled, and institutional grants and scholarships could be reduced or taken away. [1] NJ State aid (e.g., TAG, EOF) requires full-time enrollment when the aid is fully disbursed. [2]

For an explanation of your spring award, contact the Office of Financial Aid. If family circumstances or finances have changed, email or call to discuss your situation and the possibility of a re-evaluation. Appointments can be requested by email or through the chat on the Financial Aid website. In-person appointments are Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 4:30pm; questions can also be handled by phone, Webex or email. [7]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [33]

This office can help:
**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [34]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I applied to the honors program and got rejected but they said I can reapply? I don't understand what I'm supposed to do differently or when

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes. That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

If you were not accepted, you may reapply at the end of your first semester at Ramapo College. [1]

For continuing students who just completed their first semester, apply between December 1 and January 8. [2][7] You must have a 3.50 GPA from the fall semester. [7] Email PDFs of these materials to honors@ramapo.edu with the headline “Honors Application”: [7]
1. An admission essay, 800 words or less, answering the prompt: “Most people belong to many different communities; groups defined by (among other things) shared geography, religion, ethnicity, income, cuisine, interests, race, ideology, or intellectual heritage. Choose one of the communities to which you belong and describe that community and your place within it.” [7]
2. One letter of recommendation from a Ramapo College faculty member. Ask them to submit it to Director, Erin Augis (eaugis@ramapo.edu). The letter should demonstrate personal knowledge of your intellectual independence and capacity for engaged learning. [7]
3. A previously completed essay or project from your first semester at Ramapo College that demonstrates the qualities required for admission. Include a description of the assignment and class it was created for. Attach it as a regular PDF, not an embedded link. [7]

The program considers both quantitative and qualitative measures, including your academic performance, essay, recommendation, and work sample. [2][7]

answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes. That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

If you were not accepted, you may reapply at the end of your first semester at Ramapo College. [1]

For continuing students who just completed their first semester, apply between December 1 and January 8. [2][7] You must have a 3.50 GPA from the fall semester. [7] Email PDFs of these materials to honors@ramapo.edu with the headline “Honors Application”: [7]
1. An admission essay, 800 words or less, answering the prompt: “Most people belong to many different communities; groups defined by (among other things) shared geography, religion, ethnicity, income, cuisine, interests, race, ideology, or intellectual heritage. Choose one of the communities to which you belong and describe that community and your place within it.” [7]
2. One letter of recommendation from a Ramapo College faculty member. Ask them to submit it to Director, Erin Augis (eaugis@ramapo.edu). The letter should demonstrate personal knowledge of your intellectual independence and capacity for engaged learning. [7]
3. A previously completed essay or project from your first semester at Ramapo College that demonstrates the qualities required for admission. Include a description of the assignment and class it was created for. Attach it as a regular PDF, not an embedded link. [7]

The program considers both quantitative and qualitative measures, including your academic performance, essay, recommendation, and work sample. [2][7]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [30]
